A1.justification: The shared authors, shape-conditioned synthesis pipeline and Pix3D application establish continuity despite substantial retitling and revision. All supplied pages are readable. However, v1 includes Appendices A–F, whereas v2 references supplementary material absent from its 12-page PDF, limiting comparison of supplementary details and results.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-data quality measurements and AtlasNet/Mesh R-CNN experiments on Pix3D (Tables 2–7), with additional results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction comparisons and ablations on Pix3D (Tables 1–3), plus qualitative evaluations on ObjectNet, OfficeHome and PACS (Figure 9).

M1.justification: v1 proposes data synthesis for existing reconstructors. v2 adds a DPT-based model predicting camera intrinsics, depth, visible/occluder masks and cross-attention occupancy, with text conditioning and new losses (Section 3). Independently generated and composited backgrounds become object-aware outpainting; random erasing in v1 Appendix B becomes Copy-Paste object occlusion in v2 Section 4.4.

E1.justification: v1 uses ShapeNet/ABO for reconstruction experiments and Objaverse-XL/MeshDiffusion for synthesis demonstrations, with evaluation on Pix3D. v2 expands training coverage to over 1,000 categories using ShapeNetCore.v2 and Objaverse-LVIS. It retains Pix3D and adds qualitative evaluation on ObjectNet, OfficeHome and PACS (Figure 9), substantially broadening evaluated object and image coverage.

E2.justification: v1 compares pretraining alternatives using ObjectDR, PyTorch3D and Blender renderings on AtlasNet/Mesh R-CNN, and includes a qualitative CRM comparison (Figure E2). v2 instead evaluates LRM and ZeroShape, each with SAM alone or SAM plus pix2gestalt, against the new reconstruction model (Table 1 and Figure 8).

E3.justification: v1 evaluates pretraining and fine-tuning on explicit Pix3D S1/S2 splits, including pretraining-only controls. v2 uses a new zero-shot evaluation design with Marching Cubes extraction, segmentation/completion preprocessing for baselines, and F-scores at multiple thresholds alongside CD. ICP alignment and 10K-point sampling carry over from v1's AtlasNet protocol; training scale and occlusion augmentation also change substantially.

E4.justification: v1 analyzes guidance-injection steps, synthesis scale and appearance/background randomization (Figure 7, Tables 5–6 and Appendix D). v2 adds VLM-versus-ground-truth category comparisons and ablations of auxiliary depth loss, occluder processing and text prompts (Tables 2–3). The earlier quantitative synthesis analyses are not present in the supplied v2; the initial-guidance illustration in Figure 6 is retained.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. v1's random seeds control image synthesis rather than statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The AtlasNet/Mesh R-CNN and synthetic-quality result tables in v1 are replaced by new reconstruction comparisons and ablations. v2 Table 1 reports FS@τ/CD of 38.2/0.097 for category-agnostic prediction and 39.1/0.095 for category-specific prediction, versus 33.6/0.110 for ZeroShape with SAM and pix2gestalt. Changed models and protocols prevent direct performance comparison with v1.

T1.justification: v2 adds explicit mathematical definitions of category-conditioned feature modulation (Equation 1) and mask-gated depth unprojection into visible 3D geometry (Equation 2). v1 provides synthesis pseudocode but lacks this reconstruction formulation. The mathematical addition is limited; neither version develops theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from scalable ObjectDR synthesis, the diversity–fidelity trade-off and improved pretraining to a unified occlusion-aware reconstructor claiming state-of-the-art zero-shot results with fewer parameters. Data synthesis remains a contribution, but v1's highlighted 23.6% scale-up claim is replaced by claims about integrated reconstruction without external segmentation or completion.

C2.justification: v1 emphasizes synthesis fidelity, annotation noise and their effects on pretraining. v2 adds explanations involving depth and semantic priors, possible pix2gestalt–LRM incompatibility, and limitations from image truncation and inconsistent object definitions such as beds with or without pillows. The segmentation-error and occlusion critique already present in v1 Appendix E.2 is retained.

D1.justification: v1 provides rendering, sampling, filtering and training recipes in Section 4 and Appendices A–C, plus a project-page link. v2 adds architecture dimensions, 224×224 inputs, two cross-attention layers and named depth/VLM components (Section 3.4). However, its supplied PDF lacks a comparable training recipe, numerical F-score threshold and project link; the referenced supplementary details are unavailable.

R1.justification: v2 reorganizes positioning around generative versus regression-based zero-shot reconstruction and claims the first regression-based zero-shot reconstruction in the wild (Section 2). It adds works including LRM, ZeroShape, pix2gestalt and object-aware background generation, and introduces a discussion of generative models using 3D assets. This substantially changes positioning beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and much of the narrative are rewritten around the unified reconstruction model. The synthesis-centered Method section becomes a separate Data Synthesis section following the new model description, while experiments and limitations are reorganized. The earlier appendix's segmentation critique is incorporated into the main motivation.

P2.justification: v2 changes the single-column layout to two columns and replaces much of the figure/table suite. It adds a reconstruction architecture diagram (Figure 3), revises the synthesis pipeline diagram (Figure 5), and introduces reconstruction-comparison and component-ablation tables. The initial-guidance illustration is reused, while many earlier synthesis-analysis displays are absent from the supplied v2.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the reconstruction argument with quantitative LRM/ZeroShape comparisons and model-component tests (Tables 1–3), extending v1's qualitative critique of segmentation pipelines. However, the supplied version lacks v1's quantitative synthesis-quality and scaling validation and comparably complete training documentation. Its referenced supplement is absent, and the F-score threshold and Pix3D test selection remain unspecified. These gains and reduced verifiability prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
